subject: Throughput & Latency qualification — EdgeMark follow-up and cost levers
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@edgemark.ai>, infra@edgemark.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Throughput & Latency qualification — EdgeMark follow-up and cost levers

Hi Samantha (and infra team),

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion and clear targets. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we can line up a short qualification (bench) run next week.

Summary of requirements you shared
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end generation <= 350 ms for single-turn responses up to ~256 tokens (realistic for your customer-facing autocomplete flow).
- Sustained throughput: ~80–120 QPS for prediction endpoint (burst to 180 QPS for short windows).
- Concurrency: expected 30–45 concurrent streams during peak; many of your requests will use streaming (progressive tokens to client).
- Quality: insist on current accuracy for ranking/intent models; willing to trade some model size for latency but not for core NLU quality.

Key performance & cost levers we recommend to get you within SLOs
1) Continuous batching: automatic batching of small requests but with strict per-request latency caps; we'll tune batching windows to avoid adding tail latency. Good win for throughput-dependent cost reduction.
2) Prefix/KV caching: for high repetition or templated prompts (auto-complete), prefix caching reduces repeated compute dramatically.
3) Quantization profiles: we can try int8 or 4-bit quantized variants for the 7B family; 7B-quant often reduces latency ~25–40% on Ampere-class GPUs with small accuracy delta. For top-end quality, keep 13B in a separate fallback pool.
4) Model routing & variants: split traffic by intent/route — low-latency routes to 7B-quant; batch/analytics jobs to 13B or non-quantized variants.
5) Streaming chunk size and KV strategy: use 64-token chunking for steady streaming; larger chunks give better throughput but increase payload latency.

Immediate asks / next steps
- Confirm: are you OK with a pilot that routes 60% of live traffic to a 7B-quant route and 40% to a higher-quality 13B pool during the test? (we can change ratios).
- Redwood will run a 6-hour qualification run that simulates your RPS and concurrency mix. We’ll deliver: p50/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and cost-per-1M tokens for the tested configs.
- Please provide: a representative sample of prompt shapes (anonymized) and the ratio of short vs long completions (we used 70% short < 64 tokens, 30% up to 256 in our model).
- Target dates: bench run ready by Tue 2027-02-16 if we have prompts by EOD Mon 2027-02-15.

Attachments: edgemark-qual-matrix.csv (template), redwood-cost-model.xlsx (cost scenarios), redwood-sla-draft.pdf (SLA language draft).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule the bench and loop in Rishi and Marissa for the configuration review.

Thanks,
Olga

Samantha — quick note from the commercial side:

We’re happy to offer a short pilot credit (1 month, capped) so you can test under real traffic with minimal cost risk. If the bench shows the config meets your p95 latency and throughput, we’ll propose a mutual action plan and an SOW for dedicated capacity (if you want isolation) or a production routing plan on hosted.

Proposed immediate plan
- Confirm prompts and traffic mix by EOD Mon 2027-02-15.
- Bench run Tue 02/16 (Redwood infra runs tests; observers from EdgeMark welcome).
- Quick sync Thu 02/18 for results and recommended config.

Ben
Account Executive — Redwoods Sales
ben@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Samantha Lee <samantha@edgemark.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra@edgemark.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput & Latency qualification — EdgeMark follow-up and cost levers

Thanks, Olga and Ben — that all looks good to me.

Confirmations:
- Pilot routing split is fine (60/40) for the bench pass.
- We’ll anonymize and upload a representative prompt sample to the Drive link you shared by EOD Mon 2027-02-15.
- Observers: I’ll add our lead infra (Ken Park) to the bench session; he’ll be on the call Tue morning.

One small ask: for the streaming path we want first-token latency (TTFT) to be as low as possible — is the 64-token chunking you recommended adjustable per route? We have a couple of microservices that need sub-120ms TTFT for token 1.

Also attaching the engineering contact list and a small traffic heatmap so you can tune the concurrency profile.

Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Platform — EdgeMark
samantha@edgemark.ai | (212) 555-0102

Attachments referenced: edgemark-engineering-contacts.csv, edgemark-traffic-heatmap.png

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@edgemark.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, infra@edgemark.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput & Latency qualification — EdgeMark follow-up and cost levers

Perfect, thanks Samantha. Quick answers and final notes before the bench: 

- Chunking per route: yes — we can set TTFT-sensitive routes to 16–32 token chunking for first-token responsiveness; tradeoff is slightly higher GPU overhead and lower throughput efficiency. We’ll add a specific route config for the microservice(s) you flagged.
- For the pilot we’ll run two configs in parallel:
  * Config A (latency-optimized): 7B-quant, continuous batching tuned to maintain p95 <= 350ms, streaming chunk 32 tokens for TTFT-critical routes.
  * Config B (quality fallback): 13B (non-quantized), larger batching for higher throughput when latency window permits.

Deliverables after the 6-hour run (we’ll publish a one-page summary + raw CSV): p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost-per-1M tokens, and suggestions for caching/kv-hit thresholds.

Action items assigned:
- EdgeMark: upload prompts + traffic heatmap (Samantha) — due EOD Mon 02/15.
- Redwood: bench config and run (Olga, Rishi) — target Tue 02/16.
- Redwood Product: prepare a short note on quantization accuracy delta for your specific prompt set (Marissa) — will attach to results.

I’ll schedule the run invite and Slack channel now; Ben, I’ll follow up with a short pilot credit note for your approval.

Talk soon — looking forward to the test.

Olga
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
